page: Microsoft Azure GS4-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 459 GB drive, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing speed. The Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor delivers poor single-core performance, placing in the bottom 10% on stress-ng and Geekbench tests, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints, with large-block write speeds scoring in the bottom 10%, though small-block cached read bandwidth remains average.

Despite the lower CPU performance, the GS4-8 maintains average performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, achieving 6.85 million operations per second. This profile makes the server suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU compute, such as caching layers, in-memory databases, and moderate database hosting. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density provides a specialized resource allocation, though the older CPU architecture limits its utility for compute-heavy tasks.
